claim: The retina is the only neural tissue whose physiology and pathology can be non-invasively probed by optical microscopy.
source: The retina, behind the transparent optics of the eye, is the only neural tissue whose physiology and pathology can be non-invasively probed by optical microscopy.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract about the unique accessibility of the retina.

claim: The aberrations intrinsic to the mouse eye prevent high-resolution investigation of retinal structure and function in vivo.
source: The aberrations intrinsic to the mouse eye, however, prevent high-resolution investigation of retinal structure and function in vivo.
evidence: This statement is made in the abstract as a motivation for the study.

claim: Adaptive optics is essential for resolving putative synaptic structures in the mouse retina in vivo.
source: we found that adaptive optics (AO), by measuring and correcting ocular aberrations, is essential for resolving putative synaptic structures and achieving three-dimensional cellular resolution in the mouse retina in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated with experimental data in Figure 1C.

claim: Adaptive optics is essential for achieving three-dimensional cellular resolution in the mouse retina in vivo.
source: we found that adaptive optics (AO), by measuring and correcting ocular aberrations, is essential for resolving putative synaptic structures and achieving three-dimensional cellular resolution in the mouse retina in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated with experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: AO-2PFM characterized microvascular lesions with sub-capillary details in a proliferative vascular retinopathy model.
source: Applying AO-2PFM to longitudinal retinal imaging in transgenic models of retinal pathology, we characterized microvascular lesions with sub-capillary details in a proliferative vascular retinopathy model
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated with experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: Lidocaine effectively suppresses retinal ganglion cell hyperactivity in a retinal degeneration model.
source: we characterized microvascular lesions with sub-capillary details in a proliferative vascular retinopathy model, and found Lidocaine to effectively suppress retinal ganglion cell hyperactivity in a retinal degeneration model.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated with experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: Retina is a layered tissue in the back of the eye that transduces light into electrochemical signals.
source: Retina is a layered tissue in the back of the eye that transduces light into electrochemical signals to be further processed by the brain for visual perception and cognition (Kandel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The retina is one of the most energy-demanding tissues.
source: As one of the most energy-demanding tissues, the retina is metabolically sustained by an intricate vasculature with several laminar plexuses (Selvam et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation.

claim: The retina is metabolically sustained by an intricate vasculature with several laminar plexuses.
source: As one of the most energy-demanding tissues, the retina is metabolically sustained by an intricate vasculature with several laminar plexuses (Selvam et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement supported by a citation.

claim: Vascular and neuronal abnormalities in the retina are associated with both ocular and systemic diseases.
source: Vascular and neuronal abnormalities in the retina are associated with both ocular (Schachat et al., 2017) and systemic diseases (Cheung et al., 2017; London et al., 2013; Lechner et al., 2017)
evidence: This is a statement supported by multiple citations.

claim: Mouse models have been widely utilized for mechanistical studies of retinal diseases.
source: With well-developed genetics and similar physiology to the human retina, mouse models have been widely utilized for mechanistical studies of retinal diseases.
evidence: This is a statement of established practice in the field.

claim: The retina is the only part of the nervous system that can be probed non-invasively by optical imaging.
source: Behind highly transparent mouse eye optics (i.e. cornea and crystalline lens), the retina is uniquely accessible to light and the only part of the nervous system that can be probed non-invasively by optical imaging.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about retinal accessibility.

claim: Recent advances in mouse genetics have enabled fluorescence microscopy investigations of vasculature in the mouse retina.
source: Recent advances in mouse genetics have enabled fluorescence microscopy investigations of vasculature (Ivanova et al., 2021) as well as neurons and glial cells (Jo et al., 2018; Martersteck et al., 2017; Eme-Scolan and Dando, 2020) of the mouse retina.
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: Recent advances in mouse genetics have enabled fluorescence microscopy investigations of neurons and glial cells in the mouse retina.
source: Recent advances in mouse genetics have enabled fluorescence microscopy investigations of vasculature (Ivanova et al., 2021) as well as neurons and glial cells (Jo et al., 2018; Martersteck et al., 2017; Eme-Scolan and Dando, 2020) of the mouse retina.
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: Two-photon fluorescence microscopy utilizing near-infrared excitation is particularly suited for retinal imaging.
source: Among fluorescence microscopy techniques, two-photon fluorescence microscopy (2PFM) (Denk et al., 1990) utilizing near-infrared (NIR) excitation is particularly suited for retinal imaging.
evidence: This is a statement supported by citation and reasoning about the technique's properties.

claim: 2PFM has intrinsic optical sectioning capability that permits depth-resolved three-dimensional imaging throughout the retina.
source: Its intrinsic optical sectioning capability permits depth-resolved three-dimensional (3D) imaging throughout the retina.
evidence: This is a statement about the technical capabilities of 2PFM.

claim: Retinal photoreceptors are minimally responsive to NIR light.
source: With the retinal photoreceptors minimally responsive to NIR light, 2PFM is also an ideal tool for functional studies of retina (Euler et al., 2002; Baden et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: 2PFM is an ideal tool for functional studies of retina.
source: With the retinal photoreceptors minimally responsive to NIR light, 2PFM is also an ideal tool for functional studies of retina (Euler et al., 2002; Baden et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations and reasoning.

claim: The optics of the mouse eye introduce severe aberrations to the NIR excitation light.
source: However, as a far-from-perfect imaging system, the optics of the mouse eye introduce severe aberrations to the NIR excitation light, preventing high-resolution visualization of subcellular features in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the optical properties of the mouse eye, supported by the study's findings.

claim: The vast majority of microscopy studies have been carried out ex vivo on dissected retinas.
source: As a result, the vast majority of microscopy studies have been carried out ex vivo on dissected retinas, preventing longitudinal investigations of retinal pathology under physiological conditions.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field.

claim: Adaptive optics actively measures and corrects for optical aberrations.
source: Adaptive optics (AO) is a collection of technologies that actively measure and correct for optical aberrations (Hampson et al., 2021)
evidence: This is a definition supported by a citation.

claim: AO has been applied to optical microscopy for high-resolution imaging of neural tissues.
source: Adaptive optics (AO) is a collection of technologies that actively measure and correct for optical aberrations (Hampson et al., 2021), and has been applied to optical microscopy for high-resolution imaging of neural tissues (Ji, 2017; Rodríguez and Ji, 2018).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: AO has been combined with ophthalmological imaging modalities to restore diffraction-limited imaging performance for the human retina.
source: It has also been combined with ophthalmological imaging modalities to restore diffraction-limited imaging performance for the human retina (Liang et al., 1997; Akyol et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: AO has been applied to in vivo imaging of the mouse retina.
source: Because of the severe aberrations of the mouse eye, AO has also been applied to in vivo imaging of the mouse retina (Palczewska et al., 2014; Biss et al., 2007; Alt et al., 2010; Geng et al., 2012; Sharma et al., 2013; Wahl et al., 2016; Wahl et al., 2019; Qin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement supported by multiple citations.

claim: There are disagreements in the reported spatial resolutions for AO imaging of the mouse retina.
source: However, there are disagreements in the reported spatial resolutions (Palczewska et al., 2014; Biss et al., 2007; Alt et al., 2010; Geng et al., 2012; Sharma et al., 2013; Wahl et al., 2016; Wahl et al., 2019; Qin et al., 2020), characteristics and magnitude of aberration (Palczewska et al., 2014; Biss et al., 2007; Alt et al., 2010; Wahl et al., 2016; Wahl et al., 2019; Qin et al., 2020), and the effectiveness of AO (Biss et al., 2007; Alt et al., 2010; Wahl et al., 2016; Wahl et al., 2019; Qin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about discrepancies in the literature, supported by citations.

claim: There are disagreements in the reported characteristics and magnitude of aberration in the mouse eye.
source: However, there are disagreements in the reported spatial resolutions (Palczewska et al., 2014; Biss et al., 2007; Alt et al., 2010; Geng et al., 2012; Sharma et al., 2013; Wahl et al., 2016; Wahl et al., 2019; Qin et al., 2020), characteristics and magnitude of aberration (Palczewska et al., 2014; Biss et al., 2007; Alt et al., 2010; Wahl et al., 2016; Wahl et al., 2019; Qin et al., 2020), and the effectiveness of AO (Biss et al., 2007; Alt et al., 2010; Wahl et al., 2016; Wahl et al., 2019; Qin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about discrepancies in the literature, supported by citations.

claim: There are disagreements in the reported effectiveness of AO for mouse retinal imaging.
source: However, there are disagreements in the reported spatial resolutions (Palczewska et al., 2014; Biss et al., 2007; Alt et al., 2010; Geng et al., 2012; Sharma et al., 2013; Wahl et al., 2016; Wahl et al., 2019; Qin et al., 2020), characteristics and magnitude of aberration (Palczewska et al., 2014; Biss et al., 2007; Alt et al., 2010; Wahl et al., 2016; Wahl et al., 2019; Qin et al., 2020), and the effectiveness of AO (Biss et al., 2007; Alt et al., 2010; Wahl et al., 2016; Wahl et al., 2019; Qin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about discrepancies in the literature, supported by citations.

claim: Previous papers reported cellular resolution without AO.
source: For example, whereas previous papers reported cellular resolution without AO, a recent AO-2PFM study (Qin et al., 2020) reported extremely large aberrations in the mouse eye and found AO to be required in order to resolve microvasculature and cell bodies in 2D in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about previous findings in the literature.

claim: A recent AO-2PFM study reported extremely large aberrations in the mouse eye.
source: For example, whereas previous papers reported cellular resolution without AO, a recent AO-2PFM study (Qin et al., 2020) reported extremely large aberrations in the mouse eye and found AO to be required in order to resolve microvasculature and cell bodies in 2D in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about a specific study, supported by citation.

claim: A recent AO-2PFM study found AO to be required to resolve microvasculature and cell bodies in 2D in vivo.
source: For example, whereas previous papers reported cellular resolution without AO, a recent AO-2PFM study (Qin et al., 2020) reported extremely large aberrations in the mouse eye and found AO to be required in order to resolve microvasculature and cell bodies in 2D in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about a specific study, supported by citation.

claim: Using a carefully engineered 2PFM and following an optimized sample preparation procedure, two-dimensional cellular resolution imaging performance in the mouse retina was achieved without AO.
source: Using a carefully engineered 2PFM and following an optimized sample preparation procedure, we were able to achieve two-dimensional (2D) cellular resolution imaging performance in the mouse retina without AO.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and demonstrated with experimental data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: AO was essential for synaptic, subcellular, and three-dimensional cellular resolution imaging of the mouse retina.
source: For synaptic, subcellular, and three-dimensional (3D) cellular resolution imaging of the mouse retina, AO was essential in improving image brightness, contrast, and resolution.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and demonstrated with experimental data in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: AO improved image brightness, contrast, and resolution for synaptic, subcellular, and 3D cellular resolution imaging of the mouse retina.
source: For synaptic, subcellular, and three-dimensional (3D) cellular resolution imaging of the mouse retina, AO was essential in improving image brightness, contrast, and resolution.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and demonstrated with experimental data.

claim: AO enabled characterization of retinal vascular lesions with sub-capillary details over multiple days.
source: In our model of proliferative vascular retinopathy, AO enabled us to, for the first time, characterize retinal vascular lesions with sub-capillary details over multiple days and observe cell migration in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and demonstrated with experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: AO enabled observation of cell migration in vivo in a proliferative vascular retinopathy model.
source: In our model of proliferative vascular retinopathy, AO enabled us to, for the first time, characterize retinal vascular lesions with sub-capillary details over multiple days and observe cell migration in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and demonstrated with experimental data in Figure 5G.

claim: AO allowed high-fidelity interrogation of pharmacologically modified hyperactivity of retinal ganglion cells in a retinal degeneration model.
source: In our model of retinal degeneration, AO allowed high-fidelity interrogation of pharmacologically modified hyperactivity of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), indicating AO-2PFM as a promising tool evaluating retinal pharmacology in vivo.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the introduction and demonstrated with experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: The AO-2PFM was built upon a homebuilt 2PFM incorporated with a direct-wavefront-sensing-based AO module.
source: The AO-2PFM was built upon a homebuilt 2PFM (Figure 1A) incorporated with a direct-wavefront-sensing-based AO module, as described in detail previously (Li et al., 2020b).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental setup, supported by citation.

claim: 920 nm output from a femtosecond Ti:Sapphire laser was used for two-photon excitation.
source: Briefly, 920 nm output from a femtosecond Ti:Sapphire laser (Coherent, Chameleon Ultra II) was expanded (2×, Thorlabs, GBE02-B) after a Pockel Cell (ConOptics, 350–80-LA-02-BK).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental setup.

claim: The focal plane position of two-photon excitation in the mouse retina was controlled by an electrically tunable lens.
source: The focal plane position of two-photon excitation in the mouse retina was controlled by an electrically tunable lens (ETL; Optotune, EL-16–40-TC-VIS-5D-C), which was conjugated to the DM (by L5-L6, FL = 175 and 400 mm; Edmund Optics, 49–363-INK and Newport, PAC090).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental setup.

claim: System aberrations in the two-photon illumination path were measured with a modal AO method and corrected before image acquisition.
source: For all experiments, system aberrations in the two-photon illumination path were measured with a modal AO method and corrected before image acquisition (Materials and methods; 'No AO' images: system aberration correction only).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedure.

claim: Aberrations introduced by the ETL at different control currents minimally affected image quality.
source: We found that aberrations introduced by the ETL at different control currents minimally affected image quality and that axial focal shift varied linearly with ETL current while field-of-view (FOV) size remained mostly constant.
evidence: This is a finding from characterization experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Axial focal shift varied linearly with ETL current.
source: We found that aberrations introduced by the ETL at different control currents minimally affected image quality and that axial focal shift varied linearly with ETL current while field-of-view (FOV) size remained mostly constant.
evidence: This is a finding from characterization experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Field-of-view size remained mostly constant with different ETL currents.
source: We found that aberrations introduced by the ETL at different control currents minimally affected image quality and that axial focal shift varied linearly with ETL current while field-of-view (FOV) size remained mostly constant.
evidence: This is a finding from characterization experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: A custom-designed 0-diopter contact lens in combination with eye gel reduced aberrations.
source: We discovered that a custom-designed 0-diopter contact lens (CL; design parameters in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) in combination with a single application of eye gel between the CL and the cornea reduced aberrations, prevented cataract formation, and improved wavefront sensing and imaging for hours (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from optimization experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: A custom-designed 0-diopter contact lens in combination with eye gel prevented cataract formation.
source: We discovered that a custom-designed 0-diopter contact lens (CL; design parameters in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) in combination with a single application of eye gel between the CL and the cornea reduced aberrations, prevented cataract formation, and improved wavefront sensing and imaging for hours (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from optimization experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: A custom-designed 0-diopter contact lens in combination with eye gel improved wavefront sensing and imaging for hours.
source: We discovered that a custom-designed 0-diopter contact lens (CL; design parameters in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) in combination with a single application of eye gel between the CL and the cornea reduced aberrations, prevented cataract formation, and improved wavefront sensing and imaging for hours (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from optimization experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ocular aberrations were measured and corrected with a direct wavefront sensing method.
source: In order to achieve diffraction-limited imaging of the mouse retina in vivo, we measured and corrected ocular aberrations with a direct wavefront sensing method (Wang et al., 2014b; Wang et al., 2015), utilizing the SH sensor for wavefront measurement and the DM for wavefront correction (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method, supported by citations.

claim: After aberration correction, an 8.6× increase in signal was achieved for RGC axons.
source: The image taken without AO showed dim and distorted RGC axons; after aberration correction, we achieved an 8.6× increase in signal and proper visualization of the fine RGC axons (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: AO led to a lateral resolution that was better than ~0.8 µm for RGC axons.
source: The spatial frequency space representations of the images indicated that AO enhanced the ability of the imaging system to acquire higher resolution information and led to a lateral resolution that was better than ~0.8 µm (Figure 1B, insets).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experimental data shown in Figure 1B insets.

claim: For thin RGC processes, restoring diffraction-limited resolution led to a 10.6× increase in signal.
source: For some thin RGC processes (Figure 1C), restoring diffraction-limited resolution led to an increase in signal (by 10.6×) and contrast (Figure 1C, i)
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: AO enabled in vivo 2PFM visualization of varicosities resembling synaptic structures in the mouse retina for the first time.
source: For some thin RGC processes (Figure 1C), restoring diffraction-limited resolution led to an increase in signal (by 10.6×) and contrast (Figure 1C, i), and, for the first time, enabled in vivo 2PFM visualization of varicosities resembling synaptic structures in the mouse retina (Figure 1C, white arrowheads).
evidence: This is a primary finding from experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The axial resolution after AO correction was estimated to be 6.7 µm.
source: From the axial profile of a thin process (Figure 1C, ii), we estimated the axial resolution after AO correction to be 6.7 µm.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The lateral and axial resolution estimations were close to the theoretical diffraction-limited resolution for a fully-dilated mouse eye with 0.49 numerical aperture.
source: Both the lateral and axial resolution estimations were close to the theoretical diffraction-limited resolution for a fully-dilated mouse eye with 0.49 numerical aperture (Geng et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a comparison to theoretical values, supported by citation.

claim: Retinal vasculature supports the physiological functions of the retina.
source: Retinal vasculature supports the physiological functions of the retina.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge.

claim: Retinal vascular diseases can lead to vision loss.
source: Retinal vascular diseases can lead to vision loss.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge.

claim: Abnormalities in retinal vasculature morphology and physiology serve as important biomarkers for various cerebral and systemic diseases.
source: Abnormalities in retinal vasculature morphology and physiology serve as important biomarkers for various cerebral and systemic diseases (Patton et al., 2005; Frost et al., 2013; Ikram et al., 2013; Liew et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: After AO correction, a 2–10× enhancement in signal was observed for retinal vessels.
source: After AO correction, we observed a 2–10× enhancement in signal (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: AO's impact on signal of smaller capillaries (6–10× improvement) was more substantial than on larger vessels (2–3× improvement).
source: Comparing the line signal profiles (along the orange dashed lines, Figure 2A and B), we found that AO improved signal for all vessels while its impact on signal of smaller capillaries (Figure 2C, black asterisks; 6–10× improvement) was more substantial than on larger vessels (Figure 2C, black circles; 2–3× improvement).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Most capillaries could be resolved in 3D without AO by the optimized 2PFM, albeit at reduced contrast and resolution.
source: Despite the substantial signal improvements enabled by AO, we found that most capillaries, due to their size and sparse distribution in space, could be resolved in 3D without AO by our optimized 2PFM, albeit at reduced contrast and resolution (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: A properly designed 2PFM is capable of acquiring retinal angiograms at the level of individual capillaries.
source: Our results indicate that a properly designed 2PFM is capable of acquiring retinal angiograms at the level of individual capillaries.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results in Figure 2.

claim: AO performed at the superficial plexus was beneficial for imaging deeper layers.
source: We found that AO performed at the superficial plexus was beneficial for imaging deeper layers, with the correction at superficial depth improving signal, resolution, and contrast of deeper vasculature (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Most aberrations of the mouse eye arose from cornea and crystalline lens, instead of retina.
source: This result indicated that most aberrations of the mouse eye arose from cornea and crystalline lens, instead of retina.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observation that AO at superficial depth benefits deeper imaging.

claim: The crystalline lens of the mouse eye has a gradient refractive index distribution.
source: Because the crystalline lens of the mouse eye has a gradient refractive index distribution (Campbell and Hughes, 1981; Remtulla and Hallett, 1985), ocular aberrations should also be field dependent (Wang and Ji, 2012; Wang and Ji, 2013).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: Ocular aberrations should be field dependent.
source: Because the crystalline lens of the mouse eye has a gradient refractive index distribution (Campbell and Hughes, 1981; Remtulla and Hallett, 1985), ocular aberrations should also be field dependent (Wang and Ji, 2012; Wang and Ji, 2013).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations and reasoning.

claim: Signal improvement ('AO/No AO' pixel ratio ≥1) was found within a radius of ~216 µm when AO was performed at the FOV center.
source: We found signal improvement ('AO/No AO' pixel ratio ≥1) within a radius of ~216 µm when AO was performed at the FOV center of this mouse (Figure 2F, [1]).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: For off-center locations, the radius of signal improvement was slightly smaller than for center locations.
source: For off-center locations, this radius was slightly smaller (Figure 2F, [2] and [3]).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The mouse retina consists of multiple layers of neurons with different cell types and distinct physiological properties.
source: The mouse retina consists of multiple layers of neurons with different cell types and distinct physiological properties.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about retinal anatomy.

claim: In the early stage of retinal diseases, abnormal morphology and function are usually confined to specific cell types within a single layer.
source: In the early stage of retinal diseases, abnormal morphology and function are usually confined to specific cell types within a single layer (Hoon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citation.

claim: A single AO correction substantially improved signal and resolution for densely fluorescent Thy1-YFP-16 mouse retina.
source: A single AO correction acquired by scanning a 19×19 µm2 area centered on the red asterisk in (Figure 3A) substantially improved signal and resolution (Figure 3A and B; Figure 3—video 1).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: AO recovered higher spatial frequency information, thus improving both lateral and axial resolution.
source: 2D Fourier transforms of these retinal images indicated that AO recovered higher spatial frequency information (i.e. farther away from the center of Figure 3C and D) thus improved both lateral and axial resolution.
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The resolution enhancement was especially striking along the axial direction, allowing retinal layers to be more clearly differentiated.
source: The resolution enhancement was especially striking along the axial direction, allowing retinal layers to be more clearly differentiated by better resolving neurons at different depths (Figure 3A and B, XZ images).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Improvement in axial resolution minimizes neuropil contamination and ensures accurate characterization of the functional properties of neurons.
source: This improvement in axial resolution is especially important for functional imaging, because it minimizes neuropil contamination and ensures accurate characterization of the functional properties of neurons (Ji et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2014a; Sun et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: AO was necessary for 3D cellular resolution imaging of retinal neurons in vivo.
source: Therefore, AO was necessary for 3D cellular resolution imaging of retinal neurons in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results in Figure 3.

claim: The optimized 2PFM design and mouse preparation allowed the identification of individual neurons without AO in lateral image planes, albeit at lower signal and poorer resolution than with AO.
source: In the lateral image planes, our optimized 2PFM design and mouse preparation allowed the identification of individual neurons without AO, albeit at lower signal and poorer resolution than those achieved with AO, for inner nuclear layer, inner plexiform layer, and ganglion cell layer (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Subcellular processes could not be clearly visualized without aberration correction.
source: In contrast, subcellular processes could not be clearly visualized without aberration correction (e.g. processes in the inner plexiform layer, Figure 3E, white boxes in the middle column; more examples in Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Thy1-YFP-16 mouse eye exhibited field-dependent aberrations.
source: Similar to our vascular imaging results, the Thy1-YFP-16 mouse eye exhibited field-dependent aberrations.
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: For the Thy1-YFP-16 mouse, the effective area of AO performed at the FOV center was estimated to have a radius of ~185 µm.
source: For the Thy1-YFP-16 mouse, the effective area of AO performed at the FOV center was estimated from the 'AO/No AO' ratio map (Figure 3G) to have a radius of ~185 µm (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experimental data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: Correcting aberrations from smaller areas provided greater local signal improvement but exhibited faster decay in signal improvement over distance.
source: Quantifying and comparing AO effectiveness by their 'AO/No AO' pixel ratio maps (Figure 4A), we found that correcting aberrations from smaller areas provided greater local signal improvement but exhibited faster decay in signal improvement over distance (Figure 4B, i and ii).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Correcting aberrations from a larger area reduced signal improvement in the center but enlarged the overall area within which signal was enhanced.
source: In contrast, correcting aberrations from a larger area reduced signal improvement in the center of the area but enlarged the overall area within which signal was enhanced, which now extended over the entire imaging FOV (Figure 4B, iii and iv).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: A localized wavefront measurement is required for diffraction-limited imaging of fine structures within a small FOV.
source: Our results suggest that for diffraction-limited imaging of fine structures within a small FOV, a localized wavefront measurement is required, whereas a global wavefront measurement is preferable for 3D cellular resolution imaging over large FOVs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results in Figure 4.

claim: A global wavefront measurement is preferable for 3D cellular resolution imaging over large FOVs.
source: Our results suggest that for diffraction-limited imaging of fine structures within a small FOV, a localized wavefront measurement is required, whereas a global wavefront measurement is preferable for 3D cellular resolution imaging over large FOVs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results in Figure 4.

claim: Retinal angiomatous proliferation (RAP) is a subtype of age-related macular degeneration.
source: Retinal angiomatous proliferation (RAP), a subtype of age-related macular degeneration, is characterized by capillary proliferation that originates from the sensory retina and extends into the subretinal space (Yannuzzi et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citation.

claim: RAP is characterized by capillary proliferation that originates from the sensory retina and extends into the subretinal space.
source: Retinal angiomatous proliferation (RAP), a subtype of age-related macular degeneration, is characterized by capillary proliferation that originates from the sensory retina and extends into the subretinal space (Yannuzzi et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citation.

claim: The VLDLR-KO mouse model replicates the characteristic phenotypes of human RAP.
source: Replicating the characteristic phenotypes of human RAP, a transgenic mouse model, the very low-density lipoprotein receptor knockout (VLDLR-KO) mouse, has been employed to study the underlying mechanism of RAP.
evidence: This is a statement about the mouse model.

claim: In the VLDLR-KO model, the gene encoding VLDLR is knocked out, leading to overgrown intraretinal vasculature and subretinal neovascularization.
source: In this model, the gene encoding VLDLR, which mediates anti-angiogenic signaling in retinal vasculature, is knocked out, leading to overgrown intraretinal vasculature and subretinal neovascularization (Heckenlively et al., 2003; Hu et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: The VLDLR-KO model of proliferative vascular retinopathy has extensive focal vascular leakage.
source: In addition, fluorescein angiography revealed that the VLDLR-KO model of proliferative vascular retinopathy has extensive focal vascular leakage (Heckenlively et al., 2003; Hu et al., 2008; Li, 2007; Xia et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: The lack of sufficient spatial resolution and optical sectioning capability makes it challenging for fluorescence angiography to identify the 3D location and characterize the structure of vascular lesions in vivo.
source: However, the lack of sufficient spatial resolution and optical sectioning capability makes it challenging for fluorescence angiography to identify the 3D location and characterize the structure of the vascular lesions in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of fluorescence angiography.

claim: In the VLDLR-KO/Sca1-GFP retina, images acquired with AO revealed a disruption in the capillary endothelium where endothelial cells lined the walls of a short capillary branch but not its end face, leading to a ring-like structure.
source: Interestingly, in the VLDLR-KO/Sca1-GFP retina, images acquired with AO revealed a disruption in the capillary endothelium labeled by GFP, where the endothelial cells lined the walls of a short capillary branch but not its end face, leading to a ring-like structure (Figure 5A and C, yellow asterisks, insets i-ii; Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 5A and C.

claim: Ring-like structures were not observed in the WT/Sca1-GFP retina.
source: Such ring-like structures were not observed in the WT/Sca1-GFP retina (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Capillaries in the wildtype control had endothelial cells fully enclosing both the walls and the ends of capillary branches.
source: Whereas similarly structured capillary disruptions were observed in the VLDLR-KO/Sca1-GFP retina, consistent with the in vivo investigation, capillaries in the wildtype control had endothelial cells fully enclosing both the walls and the ends of capillary branches (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and D; Figure 5—video 3).
evidence: This is a finding from ex vivo experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and D.

claim: Dye leakage was observed around the lesion site immediately after FITC injection in the VLDLR-KO/Sca1-GFP mouse retina.
source: Immediately after dye injection, we observed dye leakage around the lesion site (Figure 5D, orange dashed area).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Neither capillary disruptions nor dye leakage were observed in the healthy WT/Sca1-GFP mouse retina after FITC injection.
source: A control experiment was carried out by introducing FITC into the healthy WT/Sca1-GFP mouse retina retro-orbitally, where neither capillary disruptions nor dye leakage were observed (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: EB persistently stained retinal tissue and the stained volume expanded over 3 days of consecutive imaging in the VLDLR-KO retina.
source: Similar to the experiments with FITC, we observed leakage in the knockout mouse retina, with EB persistently staining retinal tissue and the stained volume expanding over 3 days of consecutive imaging (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Capillary lesions were observed in the EB-stained volume, suggesting a spatial correlation between dye leakage and capillary abnormalities.
source: We observed capillary lesions (Figure 5F, insets) in the stained volume, suggesting a spatial correlation between dye leakage and capillary abnormalities.
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: GFP-positive cells within the dye-stained retinal volume were observed on the third day that were absent in previous 2 days.
source: Moreover, on the third day, we observed GFP-positive cells within the dye-stained retinal volume that were absent in previous 2 days (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The morphology of the GFP-positive cells resembled that of activated microglia.
source: The morphology of these cells resembled that of activated microglia (Joseph et al., 2021; Ozaki et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: The leakage of EB triggered local immune response and recruited ocular immune cells to the impacted area.
source: We speculated that the leakage of EB triggered local immune response and recruited ocular immune cells to the impacted area.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation of GFP-positive cells.

claim: AO was essential for 2PFM to achieve high-resolution identification and characterization of microvasculature lesions in vivo.
source: Here, AO was essential for 2PFM to achieve high-resolution identification and characterization of microvasculature lesions in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results in Figure 5.

claim: RGCs in the rd1 mouse become hyperactive after photoreceptor death caused by a mutation in the Pde6b gene.
source: RGCs in the rd1 mouse, the oldest and most widely studied animal model of retinal degeneration (Chang et al., 2002), become hyperactive after photoreceptor death caused by a mutation in the Pde6b gene (Sekirnjak et al., 2011; Telias et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: RGC hyperactivity masks light-evoked signals initiated by surviving photoreceptors and impedes remaining light-elicited behaviors.
source: Recent studies have suggested that RGC hyperactivity masks light-evoked signals initiated by surviving photoreceptors and impedes remaining light-elicited behaviors (Telias et al., 2019; Telias et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: RGC hyperactivity has been only studied ex vivo on dissected retinas.
source: However, RGC hyperactivity has been only studied ex vivo on dissected retinas (Telias et al., 2019; Cao et al., 2021), preventing longitudinal evaluation of degeneration progression and therapeutic approaches.
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: RGC hyperactivity measured ex vivo was correlated with a heightened ΔF/F of the GCaMP6s-expressing soma.
source: In terms of calcium signaling (quantified as calcium response magnitude ΔF/F, with F being baseline brightness and ΔF being the difference from baseline brightness), hyperactivity measured ex vivo was correlated with a heightened ΔF/F of the GCaMP6s-expressing soma.
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: A temporally varying firing rate led to transient fluctuations in calcium signal.
source: A temporally varying firing rate led to transient fluctuations in its calcium signal (ROI 1, Figure 6A), whereas a sustained high firing rate led to heightened fluorescence brightness without obvious transients (ROI 2, Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: A sustained high firing rate led to heightened fluorescence brightness without obvious transients.
source: A temporally varying firing rate led to transient fluctuations in its calcium signal (ROI 1, Figure 6A), whereas a sustained high firing rate led to heightened fluorescence brightness without obvious transients (ROI 2, Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: After ~20 seconds of 2% Lidocaine bath perfusion, spontaneous spiking from the RGC was largely suppressed with a ΔF/F close to 0.
source: After ~20 seconds of 2% Lidocaine bath perfusion, spontaneous spiking from the RGC was largely suppressed with a ΔF/F close to 0.
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: After ACSF washout, RGC hyperactivity partially recovered, which was associated with an increase of ΔF/F magnitude.
source: After artificial cerebrospinal fluid (ACSF) washout, RGC hyperactivity partially recovered, which was associated with an increase of ΔF/F magnitude.
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The observed time course and suppressive effect of Lidocaine application on RGC hyperactivity were consistent with ex vivo multi-electrode array (MEA) recordings.
source: The observed time course and suppressive effect of Lidocaine application on RGC hyperactivity were consistent with ex vivo multi-electrode array (MEA) recordings (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: AO increased RGC brightness by on average 4× in the rd1-Thy1-GCaMP6s mouse.
source: Through the rd1-Thy1-GCaMP6s mouse eye, AO increased RGC brightness by on average 4× and enabled high-resolution visualization of both RGC somata and their processes (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: AO enabled high-resolution visualization of both RGC somata and their processes in the rd1-Thy1-GCaMP6s mouse.
source: Through the rd1-Thy1-GCaMP6s mouse eye, AO increased RGC brightness by on average 4× and enabled high-resolution visualization of both RGC somata and their processes (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The RGCs in the rd1-Thy1-GCaMP6s mouse had dimmer fluorescence than the other lines investigated.
source: The signal increase enabled by AO was particularly important for the rd1-Thy1-GCaMP6s mouse, because the RGCs here had dimmer fluorescence than the other lines that we investigated.
evidence: This is a statement based on comparison across different mouse lines.

claim: Correcting the eye-induced aberration was essential for visualization and high-fidelity functional investigations of RGCs at cellular resolution in vivo in the rd1-Thy1-GCaMP6s mouse.
source: For these RGCs, correcting the eye-induced aberration was essential for their visualization and high-fidelity functional investigations at cellular resolution in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results in Figure 6C.

claim: Before injecting Lidocaine, slow fluctuations in the brightness of GCaMP6s-expressing RGCs were observed.
source: Before injecting Lidocaine, we observed slow fluctuations in the brightness of GCaMP6s-expressing RGCs (Figure 6D, i), similar to the slow dynamic events in RGC calcium traces measured ex vivo.
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: One minute after retro-orbital injection of Lidocaine, hyperactivities from RGCs were substantially inhibited for an hour as indicated by the reduction of RGC GCaMP6s fluorescence brightness.
source: One minute after retro-orbital injection of Lidocaine into the non-imaged eye, hyperactivities from these cells were substantially inhibited for an hour as indicated by the reduction of RGC GCaMP6s fluorescence brightness (Figure 6D, ii and iii).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Imaging the same RGCs 60 min after Lidocaine injection, partial recovery of RGC brightness was detected.
source: Imaging the same RGCs 60 min after injection (Figure 6D, iv), we detected partial recovery of RGC brightness, consistent with our ex vivo recordings after washing out.
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: This work demonstrated the first in vivo visualization of putative retinal synaptic structures.
source: By optimizing optical design and sample preparation and using direct wavefront sensing AO to correct mouse eye aberrations, we demonstrated here the first in vivo visualization of putative retinal synaptic structures
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding from Figure 1C.

claim: This work demonstrated the first in vivo identification of capillary lesions with sub-capillary details.
source: By optimizing optical design and sample preparation and using direct wavefront sensing AO to correct mouse eye aberrations, we demonstrated here the first in vivo visualization of putative retinal synaptic structures, the first in vivo identification of capillary lesions with sub-capillary details
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding from Figure 5.

claim: This work demonstrated the first in vivo detection of RGC hyperactivity and its suppression by pharmacological reagents.
source: By optimizing optical design and sample preparation and using direct wavefront sensing AO to correct mouse eye aberrations, we demonstrated here the first in vivo visualization of putative retinal synaptic structures, the first in vivo identification of capillary lesions with sub-capillary details, and the first in vivo detection of RGC hyperactivity and its suppression by pharmacological reagents.
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding from Figure 6.

claim: Using the mouse eye's optics itself to focus excitation light and collect fluorescence emission is preferable to using a standard objective lens for in vivo mouse retinal imaging.
source: For this reason, to achieve the best image quality and the largest FOV size, using mouse eye itself as the focusing element as implemented here is preferable.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from reasoning about optical aberrations.

claim: For the multiple mouse strains investigated, ocular aberrations were typically within the range of 3~5 µm peak-to-valley and 0.4~0.8 µm rms.
source: For the multiple mouse strains investigated here (i.e. wild-type (C57BL/6), Thy1-GFP line M, Thy1-YFP-16, VLDLR-KO/Sca1-GFP, WT/Sca1-GFP, and rd1-Thy1-GCaMP6s), we found that their ocular aberrations were typically within the range of 3~5 µm peak-to-valley (P-V; after removing tip, tilt, and defocus) and 0.4~0.8 µm rms (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) without notable differences in severity across strains.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: There were no notable differences in severity of ocular aberrations across the mouse strains investigated.
source: For the multiple mouse strains investigated here (i.e. wild-type (C57BL/6), Thy1-GFP line M, Thy1-YFP-16, VLDLR-KO/Sca1-GFP, WT/Sca1-GFP, and rd1-Thy1-GCaMP6s), we found that their ocular aberrations were typically within the range of 3~5 µm peak-to-valley (P-V; after removing tip, tilt, and defocus) and 0.4~0.8 µm rms (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) without notable differences in severity across strains.
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: With the carefully designed microscope and system aberration correction procedure, capillary visualization, 2D single-cell resolution, and retinal layer differentiation were achieved by only correcting system aberrations.
source: In contrast, with our carefully designed microscope and system aberration correction procedure, we achieved capillary visualization, 2D single-cell resolution, and retinal layer differentiation by only correcting system aberrations ('No AO' in our case).
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Figures 2 and 3.

claim: A well-engineered 2PFM should be sufficient for in vivo retinal imaging applications requiring only capillary and 2D cellular resolution.
source: Given that our system aberrations were much smaller than mouse ocular aberrations (Figure 1—figure supplement 3), our study indicated that a well-engineered 2PFM like ours should be sufficient for in vivo retinal imaging applications requiring only capillary and 2D cellular resolution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The specially designed 0-diopter contact lens encircled with a supportive flat base was essential for high-quality imaging by 2PFM both without and with AO.
source: One factor that strongly impacted image and wavefront sensing quality was the sample preparation procedure. We found that our specially designed 0-diopter contact lens encircled with a supportive flat base were essential for high-quality imaging by 2PFM both without and with AO (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The application of the contact lens smoothed corneal defects and reduced wavefront error of the anterior segment of the eye.
source: Similar improvement in imaging quality by 0-diopter contact lens was reported previously for in vivo optical coherence tomography imaging of the rat retina, where it was hypothesized that the application of the contact lens smoothed corneal defects and reduced wavefront error of the anterior segment of the eye (Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citation.

claim: The supportive flat base encircling the optical zone of the contact lens and the gel completely separated the eye surface from air and prevented cataract formation.
source: The supportive flat base encircling the optical zone of our contact lens (Ikeda et al., 2018) and the gel completely separated the eye surface from air and prevented cataract formation.
evidence: This is a statement about the function of the contact lens design, supported by citation.

claim: The contact lens and gel enabled high-quality SH images and accurate corrective wavefronts to be acquired throughout the experiment.
source: Together, they enabled high-quality SH images and accurate corrective wavefronts to be acquired throughout the experiment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Direct visualization of RGCs provides more sensitive readout of RGC degeneration than in vivo retinal characterization techniques such as optical coherence tomography and pattern electroretinogram.
source: As demonstrated recently with scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO) (Li et al., 2020a), direct visualization of RGCs provides more sensitive readout of RGC degeneration than in vivo retinal characterization techniques such as optical coherence tomography and pattern electroretinogram.
evidence: This is a statement supported by citation.

claim: SLO has been combined with calcium imaging to characterize the dynamic functional changes of RGCs in disease models.
source: SLO has been combined with calcium imaging to characterize the dynamic functional changes of RGCs in disease models (Yin et al., 2013; Cheong et al., 2018; Li et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: The visible excitation light utilized in SLO activates photoreceptors, requiring additional considerations in experimental designs.
source: Although the current commercial availability of SLO systems can make them more easily adoptable than our homebuilt AO-2PFM, the visible excitation light utilized in SLO activates photoreceptors, requiring additional considerations in experimental designs.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of SLO.

claim: Without correcting the wavefront distortion introduced by the ocular tissue, the resolution of SLO is limited to cellular level.
source: Without correcting the wavefront distortion introduced by the ocular tissue to both excitation and emission light, the resolution of SLO is limited to cellular level.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of SLO without AO.

claim: The NIR excitation light utilized in 2PFM minimizes photoreceptor activation.
source: In contrast, the NIR excitation light utilized in 2PFM minimizes photoreceptor activation; aberration correction by AO also enables subcellular resolution to be achieved in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of 2PFM.

claim: Aberration correction by AO enables subcellular resolution to be achieved in vivo with 2PFM.
source: In contrast, the NIR excitation light utilized in 2PFM minimizes photoreceptor activation; aberration correction by AO also enables subcellular resolution to be achieved in vivo.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of AO-2PFM, supported by the study's findings.

claim: Investigation of retinal vascular abnormalities in human applications are limited to capillary resolution.
source: Importantly, to probe microscopic early-stage pathologies, high spatial resolution is needed. In human applications, investigation of retinal vascular abnormalities are limited to capillary resolution (Jia et al., 2015; Hormel et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citations.

claim: Sub-capillary morphology and dynamics of the mouse retina were recently observed by light-sheet microscopy with ex vivo preparations.
source: Sub-capillary morphology and dynamics of the mouse retina were recently observed by light-sheet microscopy, however with ex vivo preparations (Prahst et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citation.

claim: Sub-capillary features had not been observed in the living mouse eye previously.
source: To our knowledge, sub-capillary features had not been observed in the living mouse eye previously.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the findings.

claim: AO enabled identification of capillary lesions as capillary endothelium disruptions that were associated with dye leakage in two-photon fluorescence angiograms.
source: Recovering diffraction-limited resolution, AO enabled us to identify capillary lesions as capillary endothelium disruptions that were associated with dye leakage in two-photon fluorescence angiograms.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Figure 5.

claim: The repeatable and reliable AO performance allowed tracking of the same retinal region over multiple days and imaging of cell migration at subcellular resolution.
source: Moreover, the repeatable and reliable AO performance allowed us to track the same retinal region over multiple days and image cell migration at subcellular resolution.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Figure 5.

claim: Pharmacological effects on retina are traditionally studied by electrophysiological and imaging tools on ex vivo retinal preparation, or in vivo by indirect assessments downstream in the visual pathway or through behavior test.
source: Traditionally, pharmacological effects on retina are studied by electrophysiological and imaging tools on ex vivo retinal preparation, or in vivo by indirect assessments downstream in the visual pathway or through behavior test (Telias et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a statement supported by citation.

claim: Treatment-induced photosensitization enhancement in retinal degeneration has been mainly evaluated through electrophysiology or ex vivo imaging of dissected retinas.
source: Taking retinal degeneration as an example, treatment-induced photosensitization enhancement has been mainly evaluated through electrophysiology or ex vivo imaging of dissected retinas.
evidence: This is a statement about current practices in the field.

claim: AO-2PFM enabled evaluation of how pathological RGC hyperactivity was suppressed by lidocaine at single cell level noninvasively.
source: AO-2PFM enabled us to evaluate how pathological RGC hyperactivity was suppressed by an example pharmacological agent, lidocaine, at single cell level noninvasively.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from Figure 6.

claim: AO-enabled high-sensitivity subcellular and cellular 2PFM imaging would become a highly enabling technology for pathological and pharmacological investigations of the mouse retina in vivo.
source: Together with the capability for longitudinal investigations discussed above, we envision that the AO-enabled high-sensitivity subcellular and cellular 2PFM imaging would become a highly enabling technology for pathological and pharmacological investigations of the mouse retina in vivo.
evidence: This is a forward-looking statement based on the study's findings.
